subject: Unexpected billing spike — cache-replay token inflation (investigation & next steps)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@novusanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected billing spike — investigation & next steps

Hi Elena —

Thanks for flagging the spike on your May 1 invoice. We noticed an unusual increase in token usage tied to a subset of streaming requests from your account and started a parallel investigation with infra.

Immediate actions we took:
- Throttled the affected routing group for Novus to prevent further inflation.
- Deployed a rollback/hotfix to the batching layer to stop duplicate accounting.
- Opened a billing investigation and paused any automated collection actions pending resolution.

Next steps we are taking now:
1) Finish a token-by-request reconciliation and estimate the over-count per invoice.
2) Apply a provisional credit for the estimated overage while we finalize numbers.
3) Share a short postmortem and permanent mitigations (monitoring, alerting, billing guardrails).

I don’t have the full numbers in this note, but we expect a preliminary CSV with the matched request ids within 48 hours. Marissa (cc) will coordinate the accounting/credit. Sean is looped for any SRE follow-up.

Can you confirm the best AP email to issue a credit memo to (invoice: INV-20260501)?

Thanks — sorry for the disruption. We’ll make this right.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@novusanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 11:03:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing spike — investigation & next steps

Elena —

Update and preliminary root cause: our infra team traced the anomaly to a cache-replay bug in the continuous-batching code path that affected streaming sessions between 2026-05-01T02:15:00Z and 2026-05-01T05:40:00Z. For certain sessions we incorrectly replayed prefix tokens during KV cache warmup, which led to inflated token accounting (effectively double-counting tokens for the open streams).

Estimated impact for Novus: ~1,860,000 tokens were miscounted across the window (approx. $3,200 by your pricing tier). We attached a stub CSV with the matched request ids and per-request delta: novus_token_spike_report.csv.

What we’ve done:
- Deployed a code fix that removes the replay behavior and added a gating test to prevent regressions.
- Added a billing-sanity monitor that will alert on >30% deviation from historical daily token baseline for an account.
- Flagged the affected invoice for provisional credit.

Accounting ask: we need to confirm whether Novus prefers a credit memo applied to your account or a direct refund to the card on file. Marissa (cc) can start a credit memo if that’s easiest.

Postmortem draft: https://drive.redwood.ai/postmortems/2026-05-cache-replay (internal link — we’ll share a redacted customer-facing summary).

Apologies again for the headache; we’ll ensure credits are visible in your account and follow up when fully reconciled.

— Jordan
